title: Launch Week
summary: Spend five weekdays preparing a weekend community market with a local non-profit. Problems appear across the site and the clock is running. Midweek, the plan breaks.

lines.text: Two volunteers want social media. Nobody's on deliveries or set-up, and both need cover by Saturday.

nodes.prompt: How do you split the roles?

options.label: Assign roles myself and post a checklist

reaction.line: Clear, but a couple of them look flat.

options.label: Ask who's free when, then pair people on logistics

reaction.line: I'll pair someone experienced with someone new. That's cover.

options.label: Take logistics myself so the team stays happy

reaction.line: You sure you have time for that?

lines.text: I need the fee by tomorrow. Trucks pay more, but small stalls bring the neighbours.

nodes.prompt: What vendor mix and fee do you set?

options.label: Mostly local stalls at a low fee
Mix: two trucks pay more, the rest stay cheap

reaction.line: Balanced. I can work with it.

options.label: Big-name trucks only, highest fees

lines.text: The food permit form isn't filed. The city office closes early tomorrow.

nodes.prompt: How do you handle the permit?

options.label: Drop everything and file it in person now
Theo files it; I check the form first
Pay a runner $150 to file it

lines.text: Our board wants the logo on every table, banner and bag. That was the deal.

nodes.prompt: What do you say?

options.label: Yes to everything, keep the sponsor happy
Banner and stage only, and say why
Push back: the market isn't an ad

lines.text: Ari and Jess are both on Saturday set-up. Clean-up has nobody, and Jess leaves at noon.

nodes.prompt: How do you fix the schedule?

options.label: Rebuild the rota myself tonight
Ask who can swap to clean-up, then confirm the new shifts
Leave it, sort it on the day

lines.text: Another festival offered me more for the same weekend. I need $400 extra to stay.

nodes.prompt: What do you offer Kenji?

options.label: No more money, but the best spot by the gate

reaction.line: Hm. Foot traffic is money. Deal.

options.label: Pay the extra $400 to keep Kenji
Offer $200 more and a smaller stall
Let him walk and replace him

lines.text: Only twelve families have signed up. Last year's market had sixty by now.

nodes.prompt: How do you get the word out?

options.label: Flyers through the school newsletters
Paid social ads
Ask vendors to promote it to their customers

reaction.line: I'll ask what they can share. They need the details today.

lines.text: The fridge rental fell through. Without cold storage, half the food can't be sold.

nodes.prompt: What do you do about cold storage?

options.label: Rent a pricier fridge today
Borrow the church's walk-in fridge
Cut the dairy and meat vendors

lines.text: The sponsor's gone, and most of the budget with it. I need a plan that fits what's left.

nodes.prompt: What is your recovery plan?

options.label: Run Saturday only; protect vendor access and food safety
Keep Saturday and Sunday; cut promotion, decorations and the stage
Move the market back two days and rebuild with partners
Keep the full programme and chase replacement funding

lines.text: We lost the site and the backup costs more. Everyone needs to know where to go.

nodes.prompt: Where does the market happen now?

options.label: Book the school field nearby and keep the full vendor list
Shrink into the church car park: fewer stalls, food and families first
Move the market back a week and keep the original layout

lines.text: Priya leaves Thursday. Her set-up and gate shifts on Saturday have nobody on them yet.

nodes.prompt: How do you cover Priya's shifts?

options.label: Cover the gate myself and move Theo to lead set-up
Share her shifts across the team; drop the late clean-up
Pay a college student to take her shifts

lines.text: The group chat went quiet after the news. Two people asked if it's even happening.

nodes.prompt: How do you reassure the team?

options.label: Call everyone in today: the new plan and what stays
Post a short update in the chat
Say nothing until the plan is final

lines.text: So where do we set up now? I need power for my oven and a time to unload.

nodes.prompt: What do you tell the vendors?

options.label: Send every vendor a site map and load-in times today
Walk the new site with vendors before handing out spots
Tell them to come early and sort spots on the day

reaction.line: With an oven? That won't work.

lines.text: Before I go, I want to hand over properly: the rota, the vendor contacts, the gate float.

nodes.prompt: How do you take over Priya's work?

options.label: Sit down with Priya and Theo and write it all down
Ask Priya to send her notes tonight

reaction.line: I'll try, but some of it is in my head.

options.label: Split it: the rota to Theo, the vendor contacts to me

lines.text: Everyone liked working with Priya. The new ones are asking who they report to now.

nodes.prompt: How do you steady the team?

options.label: Tell the team today who leads what from Thursday
Ask Theo to step up as lead and tell the team
Let things settle and see who steps up

lines.text: Is the market still on? I've ordered flour for two days. What do I tell my supplier?

nodes.prompt: What do you tell the vendors?

options.label: Tell them the truth today: what changes and what doesn't

reaction.line: Thank you for being straight with us.

options.label: Say everything is fine for now

reaction.line: I still need dates and stall details to plan.

options.label: Offer refunds on fees to anyone who wants out

lines.text: The credit union offers $800 if you pitch this afternoon, or $500 for a written plan. They want an answer today.

nodes.prompt: Do you go after the new partner?

options.label: Pitch it myself this afternoon
Send Dana with my one-page plan
Skip it, we have enough to do

lines.text: Families want an activity they can join without buying anything. I still don't see one. Can we make room?

nodes.prompt: How do you respond to Dana's feedback?

options.label: Ask what matters most, then add a free kids' activity

reaction.line: Thank you. Let's add a kids' corner.

options.label: Defend the plan and keep the programme as it is

reaction.line: I hear you. I still think it's off.

options.label: Say there's no time for changes now

lines.text: After the cuts we're short eight tables and two tents.

nodes.prompt: How do you cover the shortfall?

options.label: Borrow from the school and the library
Rent what's missing
Vendors bring their own tables

lines.text: 40% chance of rain Saturday morning. The gym is free, but it has less stall space.

nodes.prompt: What's the call?

options.label: Book the gym as a backup, decide Friday night
Keep the outdoor layout and accept the rain risk
Move indoors now to be safe

lines.text: I'm sorry. My supplier fell through and I can't come tomorrow.

nodes.prompt: What do you do about the gap?

options.label: Give her spot to a community group for free
Spread the other stalls out
Find a last-minute vendor at a discount

lines.text: The city called. Without the permit we get fined, or shut down Saturday.

nodes.prompt: How do you fix it now?

options.label: Pay the late fee and file today
Ask Dana to rush the filing through the non-profit

lines.text: I'm packing up. I'll do the food festival instead.

nodes.prompt: Last chance. What do you say?

options.label: Offer the extra $200 as a final compromise
Wish him well and fill the spot

issues.title: Vendors ask if it's still on

disruptions.title: The main sponsor pulls out
disruptions.text: I'm sorry. Our board has withdrawn the sponsorship, effective today. We can't fund the market.

disruptions.title: The venue cancels
disruptions.text: The site owner cancelled our booking. The replacement costs more, so there's less for the programme. We need to rework the weekend.

disruptions.title: Your lead volunteer leaves
disruptions.text: I got the paid internship. I start Thursday. Paid cover will cost us, but I can brief someone today.

quick.summary: Three weekdays to get a community market ready with a local non-profit. Problems pop up across the site and the clock is running. On Tuesday, the plan breaks.
